transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me today. I really appreciate it. 

Um, I hope I'm in the right place, but I've just been having a little trouble at work lately. I work at a dry cleaner's, and, well... I just can't seem to keep my things in order anymore. It's probably just me being a bit scatterbrained, I don't want to make it sound worse than it is! But the tickets, the receipts, my workshop notes, and the different customer jobs... they just sort of end up all piled together. And then I look at the pile and I just don't know what to handle first. 

I feel a little embarrassed even bringing it up, because I really do try my best to do a good job. I'm so sorry if that sounds silly, but...
Have you had trouble staying organized like this since you were a child?

Oh, um... well, yes, I suppose I have. I hope it doesn't make me sound like I was a bad student or anything, because I really did always try to be good! 

But... yes, even back in grade school, my teachers used to tell my mother that I was a bright girl—which was very sweet of them to say—but that I was just a little scattered. I guess I had a bad habit of talking out of turn sometimes, and... well, losing my school papers. And they'd always have to give me little reminders to finish my work. 

Is that the sort of thing you mean? I always felt so awful when they had to remind me, I really never
Do you often have trouble paying attention when someone is speaking to you directly?

Oh, dear... well, I really try to be a good listener. I know how important it is to pay attention to people. But, um... sometimes my mind does sort of wander off, even when I'm trying very hard to focus. 

Like at work, my helper will be standing right in front of me, telling me that a customer wants starch or no starch on their shirts. And I'll nod and smile, just like I'm supposed to, because I really do want her to feel heard. But then... maybe a minute later, I realize I didn't actually catch what she said, and I have to ask her to repeat it. 

I always feel so terrible when I do that. I don't want her to think I don't care about what she's saying, because I really do! I just... I don't know why it happens. Is that normal, doctor? I hope I don't sound too rude when I say that...
Do these same problems with staying organized and paying attention also cause trouble for you at home?

Oh, um... well, yes, I suppose it does spill over a little bit. I really try to keep things running smoothly, I promise I do! I don't want you to think I'm just letting everything fall apart. 

But, well, at the shop... we've had a few little mix-ups lately. Just some late orders, and maybe a little confusion with the billing here and there. And, well, I guess there have been a few tense moments with my helper and some of the customers. I always feel just awful about it, I really hate making anyone upset. 

And then, um, at church... I've actually had to step back a little bit from leading some of the event planning. I just... I think people were getting a little frustrated with me losing track of things, and I didn't want to be a burden to anyone. It's better for everyone if I just help out in the background, don't you think? I hope that makes sense, doctor. I just want to do what's best for everyone.
Do you often act or speak before thinking?

Oh, goodness... well, I really try to be polite and wait my turn, I really do! My mother always taught me it was rude to interrupt. But... I suppose sometimes I do get just a little bit ahead of myself. 

It's just that I get so eager to help, you know? Like, if my daughter is asking me something, or if a customer comes in with a question, or even when the trainer was showing me the new pressing machine... sometimes I just jump right in with the answer before they've even finished their sentence. 

I think I'm being helpful, but then... well, sometimes I find out I didn't actually let them finish, and I ended up answering the wrong thing entirely. It's so embarrassing! I always apologize right away, of course. I just feel awful when it happens, because I really don't mean to be disrespectful. Do you think that's something a lot of people struggle with, doctor? I just hope I'm not the only one who makes those silly mistakes...
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about many different things, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?

Oh, um... well, no, not really. I mean, I worry about normal things, of course, like anyone else would. I want to make sure my daughter is doing okay, and that the shop is running smoothly, and... well, just everyday things. 

But I don't think I worry about everything all the time, or for no reason at all. I try to stay positive and trust that things will work out. I don't want to be a burden on anyone by constantly fussing over things that haven't even happened. That wouldn't be very helpful of me, would it? I just try to take things one day at a time, doctor. I hope that's the right way to look at it...
